decisions.notes: IMPORTANT CAVEAT FOR THE COORDINATOR: this instrument is structurally closer to a permanent zoning ban than a typical temporary pause. Its own text ('AN ORDINANCE IMPOSING A MORATORIUM ON HIGH-IMPACT DATA CENTERS AND AMENDING THE CITY ZONING CODE TO ESTABLISH PROHIBITED USE CLASSIFICATION...') creates a permanent 'prohibited use' zoning category with no sunset date, and press coverage repeatedly calls it an outright ban ('Fairfax is only the second municipality in Iowa to pursue an outright ban on future data centers, joining Ida County'). I did not mark this REMOVE because (1) it has not even been finally adopted -- only a 3-1 first-reading vote -- so 'pending' is the honest status either way, and (2) the inventory already carries Ida County's outright ban under the same 'moratorium' framing, so removing Fairfax alone would be inconsistent without a broader policy call on how the inventory treats indefinite/no-sunset bans framed locally as moratoria. Recommend the coordinator decide that policy question once (Ida County vs. Fairfax vs. any other no-sunset rows) rather than have QA1 decide it ad hoc.
